messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager SEV2 - ALB/Ingress 5xx spike focused in euc1 (AZ-b). Multiple customer reports + synthetic checks failing. Oncall: evan. Follow the ingress incident runbook and post all mitigation steps here.

evan: I'm on. Seeing large increase in 502/504 from ALB->envoy starting ~16:02 UTC. Kicking off triage: LB target health, envoy error logs, k8s node metrics.

priya: dashboards show ALB healthy_count oscillating rapidly in AZ-b target group. 5xx rate peaked at ~30%. Envoy logs are showing frequent "upstream connection reset" and occasional TLS handshake failures to backends. No recent deploys.

zara: infra telemetry shows elevated TX errors and a rise in socket orphan connections on a handful of hosts in AZ-b between 16:00-16:06 UTC. Could be NIC driver or hypervisor scheduling. Opening cloud SR now.

evan: sample envoy snippet from a failing pod: 

```
[2026-03-15T16:03:11Z] envoy upstream reset: connection reset by peer, errno=104, while forwarding to 10.4.12.8:8443
[2026-03-15T16:03:12Z] TLS handshake failed: short read; likely remote close, status=502
```

nate: customer-impact update: Support has 7 active tickets for timeouts and streaming disconnects mainly in APAC/EU with euc1 routing. Some customers reported degraded service for uploads and webhooks. We notified affected orgs.

evan: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce AZ-b Route53 weight to limit exposure, 2) mark flapping ALB targets unhealthy so they aren't retried, 3) scale ingress in AZ-a/c, 4) cordon and drain suspect nodes in AZ-b, 5) consider temporarily lowering ALB keepalive timeout to force new connections.

priya: current Route53 weighted TTL is 45s. I can lower to 20s. Recommend moving 80% out of AZ-b initially.

zara: starting node cordon/drain for nodes showing NIC errors: azb-node-12, azb-node-19. Evicting pods now.

ops-bot: Route53 change queued: change-id CHG-4459 - weights: AZ-b=20%, AZ-a+c=80%, TTL=20s.

deploy-bot: autoscaling activity noted: ingress autoscaler increased replicas in AZ-a and AZ-c at 16:07 UTC. No application deploys.

evan: altering ALB target group healthcheck thresholds temporarily to avoid rapid flip-flopping while we drain bad hosts. Lowering healthy threshold to 2 and unhealthy threshold to 3 for stabilization.

priya: applied ALB TG change: tg-0a9b, health thresholds updated. Deregistering visibly flapping targets in AZ-b: i-0a2b3c4d, i-0456efab.

zara: cloud provider SR #CR-778900 opened. They report a suspected virtual switch (vSwitch) flapping on a ToR affecting a subset of hosts. They're investigating; initial ETA ~25 minutes.

nate: customer checks show synthetic failure rate dropped ~65% within two DNS propagation windows. Some long-lived TLS streams still show failures until client reconnects. CS notified customers with guidance to reconnect.

evan: we're also seeing ALB re-use of connections to backends causing TLS session reuse that sometimes fails mid-stream. As a protective measure, I'm lowering ALB keepalive (proxy) to 8s to break stale sessions and force fresh handshakes.

priya: submitted ALB config change: set idle_timeout_seconds=8 for affected listeners (change id ALBC-778). Monitor for additional errors.

ops-bot: ALB config change ALBC-778 applied.

zara: after node drains, reprovisioning effected nodes and cordoning problematic hardware for replacement. Ticket INFRA-7781 created to replace/retire affected instances.

evan: monitoring metrics, 5xx and target flapping improving. Keeping AZ-b at 20% to maintain observability. If 5xx in AZ-b > 10% for 5m, ops-bot will cut weight to 5%.

ops-bot: rule added: ingress_euc1b_5xx_rate > 10% for 5m -> set Route53 weight AZ-b=5%.

nate: support update - majority of impacted customers report restoration after reconnect. A handful with long-lived websocket streams required client reconnects to establish stable sessions. We've communicated a short summary.

priya: cloud provider reports partial routing mitigation at 16:26 UTC and that they've cleared an ARP table issue on the ToR. They mark routing stable but will monitor. SR CR-778900 updated.

evan: cautiously increasing AZ-b weight to 50% to test stability. Change-id CHG-4460.

ops-bot: Route53 change CHG-4460 processed. AZ-b=50%, TTL=20s.

zara: ENI TX/RX error rates back to baseline on reprovisioned hosts; node-azb-19 replaced and removed from cluster.

evan: ALB keepalive reset to default 60s after observing stable behavior for 10m and after verifying TLS handshakes succeed on fresh connections. Reverting ALB idle_timeout change (ALBC-779).

deploy-bot: autoscaler activity reduced; ingress pods stable.

nate: CS confirming final customer checks; majority report normal behavior. A couple of clients with legacy TLS stacks required client-side updates; advising account SREs to assist.

ops-bot: Route53 weights restored to baseline and TTL restored to 60s (change-id CHG-4461).

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. Actions: INFRA-7781 (replace flagged instances), SRE to review ALB keepalive interplay with envoy/TLS session reuse, product to review long-lived streaming guidance and retry semantics, CS to send detailed customer summary. Attach SR CR-778900 and ALB change logs to the incident doc.

evan: I'll take the lead on the RCA doc and collect logs/traces. Handoff to zara for follow-up infra work. Scheduling RCA review tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

zara: acknowledged. I'll coordinate instance replacements and verify kernel/NIC driver versions before returning nodes to rotation.

nate: support will send the customer-facing postmortem later today.

evan: closing thread 1 - attaching log bundle, ALB changes (ALBC-778, ALBC-779), Route53 changes (CHG-4459, CHG-4460, CHG-4461), and cloud SR CR-778900 to the incident tracker. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
